selected_evidence.summary: UFW is active and enabled with SSH allowed globally, node2 allowed to TCP/9000, and a following catch-all rejection for TCP/9000. Rules persisted through restart.
Both node2 and node3 successfully connected to node1 TCP/22 before and after node1 restarted.

selected_evidence.requirement: TCP/9000 allowed only from node2 and rejected from node3/everywhere else
selected_evidence.summary: With a live test listener, node2 received HTTP 200 while node3 received an immediate connection rejection, including after node1 rebooted.
node1 remained Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic; existing UFW 0.36.2 was used.
Boot identity changed from df9e2dce-0109-411e-b603-f616ac30be79 to 11cbaca8-ac14-4d9e-abab-ccfcca668538; UFW, SSH, and the required access policy recovered.
Boot identity changed from 37344ae4-6582-4c1f-ac5c-fcb32f67b968 to 47c80c92-795f-4630-a8f0-fa2d1ae01f0d; node2 recovered on 10.100.192.11 and retained permitted SSH/TCP-9000 connectivity.
Boot identity changed from f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3 to 9b9683f3-5371-4eaf-89c4-6e77bc587245; node3 recovered with SSH access while TCP/9000 remained rejected.
